measure: drop Aromatic amino acid exporter YddG

verdict: SALT ADAPTATION, which was the one account I did not expect. The signal is confined to the salt-tolerant half: -0.21178 (p 1.44e-03) above 5.0% NaCl against -0.06218 (p 3.35e-01) below it, a factor of 3.4. Well-studiedness is ruled out by an independently-defined characterised subset that does NOT reproduce it (optimum-known, n=1,655, p 0.44); measured composition is ruled out because holding genome size, GC and assembly completeness fixed leaves 100% of it; and no single reference moves it more than 0.76 SE. This is the reassuring answer rather than the alarming one: halotolerant membranes are compositionally distinct, which is a known biological fact and is exactly what scripts/43 found inside archaeal halophiles, where the transmembrane class also turns non-null and specificity fails. The control is not broken; it is responding to salt in the organisms that tolerate salt.
